I recently completed three of the top Christian financial education programs for churches: SeedTime’s True Financial Freedom, Dave Ramsey’s Financial Peace University, and Crown Financial’s MoneyLife.

Sources indicate that these popular programs all claim to help you get control of your finances from a biblical perspective. However, they go about it in different ways with varying teaching styles and philosophies.

In this post, I’ll provide an in-depth look at each program – breaking down the unique features, strengths, weaknesses, and what’s actually included when you buy in.

My goal is to give you the real deal on these courses so you can determine which one (if any) is the best fit for transforming your financial life in a way that aligns with your faith. Whether you’re deep in debt, building wealth, or simply trying to honor God with your money, this comparison will help guide your journey.

Let’s dive into the nitty-gritty details of each program:.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to pricing, Financial Peace University from Dave Ramsey sits in the middle. For an individual membership, it’s $69.99. They also offer bulk pricing for churches starting at around $800 for 10 memberships.

On the higher end, Seedtime’s True Financial Freedom charges $149 for an individual/couple license with regular deals making it available as low as $74. But they have some solid deals for Churches – you can get a bulk student license for as low as $48 per person if you buy multiple licenses. Or there’s an annual church subscription starting as low as $750 per year based on average attendance.

According to recent reports, the most affordable option is Crown Financial’s MoneyLife course at just $29.95 for an individual purchase. I couldn’t find any publicly listed bulk pricing for churches, but being a non-profit, I’d expect them to be the cheapest route for congregations.

But as you’ll see, there are plenty more differences beyond just the price tags when comparing what’s actually included in each program.

In a recent development, true Financial Freedom, created by Bob Lotich and his wife Linda from SeedTime, is a financial literacy video course designed for churches that strikes a beautiful balance between biblical wisdom and practical money management strategies. The program’s goal is to equip Christians with the tools and mindset they need to experience true financial freedom while making an eternal impact for God’s Kingdom.

One of the standout features of True Financial Freedom is the engaging and relatable teaching style of Bob and Linda. They share their own financial struggles and triumphs with humor, transparency, and grace, making participants feel like they’re learning from wise, caring friends rather than aloof experts. This approach creates a safe, non-judgmental environment where participants can openly discuss their financial challenges and celebrate their progress.

Industry observers note that the program offers several unique benefits, such as the “Never 100” rule (their ‘done-is-better-than-perfect’ approach to adjust spending) and the “Straight A” strategy for automating finances. These concepts are not only memorable but also highly actionable in helping participants take control of their money and build lasting wealth.

Another strength of True Financial Freedom is its emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy. Through interactive workshops, participants are guided in developing a custom blueprint that fits their unique situation, goals, and values. This approach recognizes that there’s no one-size-fits-all solution to personal finance and empowers participants to take ownership of their financial journey.

True Financial Freedom is perfect for Christians who want to learn how to thrive financially while staying grounded in the Bible. The program teaches participants how to avoid the extremes of being “so heavenly-minded they’re no earthly good” or becoming so focused on building worldly wealth that they lose sight of what truly matters.

With its grace-filled approach and practical tools, True Financial Freedom helps Christians find the balance needed to change their financial life and make a lasting difference in the world in the process.

In a recent development, financial Peace University, created by Dave Ramsey and his team at Ramsey Solutions, is a highly popular financial education program that has helped countless individuals and families get out of debt and build wealth. The program’s primary goal is to guide participants through a proven, step-by-step approach to taking control of their money and achieving financial peace.

Dave Ramsey, the face of Financial Peace University, is known for his high-energy, tough love teaching style. He delivers hard-hitting truths about money with a sense of urgency and conviction that inspires participants to take action. However, some may find his approach a bit intense or even abrasive at times, likening it to going through bootcamp. While this style resonates with some, it may not be everyone’s preferred learning environment.

Industry observers note that the cornerstone of Financial Peace University is the “Baby Steps” system, a clear, prescriptive plan for getting out of debt and building wealth. The program heavily emphasizes the debt snowball method, which involves paying off debts from smallest to largest, regardless of interest rates. This approach has proven highly effective in keeping participants motivated and helping them experience quick wins on their debt-free journey.

Sources indicate that while Financial Peace University does incorporate some biblical principles, its overall approach is more secular in nature. The program focuses primarily on the practical nuts and bolts of money management, with less emphasis on exploring the deeper spiritual implications of financial stewardship.

Industry observers note that financial Peace University is best suited for individuals and families who are drowning in debt and need a clear, actionable plan to get back on track. The program’s structured approach and intense motivation can be a lifeline for those feeling overwhelmed by their financial situation. However, those seeking a more personalized, grace-filled approach that deeply integrates biblical wisdom may find other programs more appealing.

MoneyLife, offered by Crown Financial, is a financial education program that takes a deeply biblical approach to money management. The program’s primary goal is to guide Christians in understanding and applying God’s financial principles to their lives, emphasizing the importance of seeing God as the ultimate provider and owner of all resources.

According to recent reports, one of MoneyLife’s distinguishing features is its strong focus on biblical teachings and spiritual practices related to money. The program dives deep into exploring how our financial decisions can reflect our faith and values, encouraging participants to align their money management with biblical principles. This emphasis on the spiritual aspects of finance sets MoneyLife apart from other programs that may focus more heavily on practical strategies.

In a recent development, the teaching style in MoneyLife tends to be more academic and classroom-like compared to other programs. Participants can expect a significant amount of reading materials and written assessments throughout the course. While this approach may appeal to those who prefer a studious learning environment, it may not be as engaging for individuals who thrive on interactive, video-based content.

MoneyLife offers some unique elements, such as personality assessments that help participants understand how their natural tendencies impact their financial decisions. The program also includes exercises like the transfer of ownership, which guides participants in acknowledging God’s ultimate ownership of their resources. These introspective activities can be powerful tools for reshaping participants’ mindsets and habits around money.

However, one potential drawback of MoneyLife is that its emphasis on biblical principles and spiritual practices may come at the expense of providing highly actionable, practical financial strategies.

MoneyLife is ideal for Christians who are seeking a deeply biblical understanding of money management and are willing to engage in a more studious, reflective learning process. The program is well-suited for those who want to explore the spiritual foundations of financial stewardship and align their money habits with their faith. However, those primarily looking for a simple and easy financial strategy or a more interactive learning experience may find other programs that better fit their needs.

Having gone through all 3 programs, here is my personal experience and recommendations:.

Industry observers note that I can honestly say that True Financial Freedom was a life-changing experience. Bob and Linda’s warm, relatable teaching style made me feel like I was learning from trusted friends who truly cared about my success. The program’s emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy was a game-changer for me, as it helped me develop a plan that fit my unique situation and goals.

In a recent development, personally, True Financial Freedom struck that balance better than any of the other programs on the list and gave me the strategy to move forward. My savings, giving, and earning have all increased in significant ways since taking the program.

For those who are drowning in debt and need a clear, structured proposal to get out, I highly recommend Financial Peace University. Dave Ramsey’s no-nonsense approach and the step-by-step “Baby Steps” system can provide the motivation and direction needed to tackle debt head-on. The debt snowball method, in particular, has helped countless people experience quick wins and build momentum on their debt-free journey. Just be prepared for a more intense, boot camp-style learning environment.

If you’re seeking a program that deeply explores the biblical principles behind money management, Crown’s MoneyLife might be the right fit for you. The program’s emphasis on spiritual practices and aligning your finances with your faith can be incredibly powerful for those who want to grow in their understanding of God’s perspective on wealth. However, be prepared for a more academic, reading-intensive learning experience and less focus on highly practical, actionable strategies.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the best program for you will depend on your unique financial situation, learning style, and personal goals. If you’re looking for a grace-filled, practical approach that helps you thrive in God’s Kingdom while making an eternal impact, I highly recommend True Financial Freedom. If you need a structured, intensive plan to get out of debt fast, Financial Peace University could be your best bet. And if you desire a deep dive into the biblical foundations of money management, MoneyLife is worth considering.

Sources indicate that regardless of which program you choose, the most vital thing is to take action and invest in your financial education. By doing so, you’ll be better equipped to handle the resources God has entrusted to you and experience the joy and freedom that comes from aligning your finances with your faith.

Passing the 1% Rule Isn’t Enough – Check a Rental’s Cash Flow Before You Offer

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Run a rental’s numbers yourself before you offer: what it nets each month after every expense and the mortgage, what you earn on the cash you put in, and how well its income covers the loan.
  • A rental can pass the 1% rule and still leave you almost nothing each month.
  • According to recent reports, say a $210,000 house rents for $2,100, exactly 1% of its price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Run a rental’s numbers yourself before you offer: what it nets each month after every expense and the mortgage, what you earn on the cash you put in, and how well its income covers the loan. The 1% rule, monthly rent at 1% of the price, only tells you which listings deserve that math.

A rental can pass the 1% rule and still leave you almost nothing each month. A listing’s projected return uses someone else’s assumptions, not yours.

According to recent reports, say a $210,000 house rents for $2,100, exactly 1% of its price. Taxes, insurance, repairs, savings for major replacements like a roof, and rent lost to empty months come to $9,600 a year. You put down 20%, or $42,000, pay $6,000 in closing costs, and borrow the other $168,000 on a 30-year investment-property loan at 8%.

A year’s rent minus every cost but the mortgage is the net operating income, here $15,600. Divide it by the price for the cap rate, 7.4%. The $1,233 monthly loan payment leaves $67 a month of cash flow, or $807 a year, which is a 1.7% cash-on-cash return on the $48,000 you put in. Many lenders check a version of the debt service coverage ratio, net operating income divided by a year of loan payments, and here it’s 1.05, barely above the 1.0 at which the income just covers the loan. Pay a property manager 8% of the rent, and you lose $101 a month.

Before you offer, swap each of the listing’s assumptions for your own:.

Compare your total with the 50% rule, which puts every cost but the mortgage at about half the rent. A total far below half the rent is a sign you missed a cost.

Recent findings suggest that last, rerun the cash flow with an extra month empty, with rent 10% lower, and with a new roof in year one. Offer no more than the price at which the cash flow stays above zero in the first two cases, and keep enough cash on hand to replace the roof.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pour laundry detergent to the fill line your label gives for your load size, not to the brim of the cap, and the same jug lasts for more loads. In the bathroom, use a small dab of shampoo, a pea-size bit of toothpaste, and a foaming pump filled with soap thinned with water.

Every extra splash of detergent or squeeze of shampoo is product you paid for and then rinsed down the drain.

Industry observers note that the dose on a detergent label is set for typical wash conditions and gives the best cleaning, says the American Cleaning Institute, the trade group for cleaning-product makers. Pour past it for an ordinary load and the jug just empties sooner. Too much detergent can even leave residue on your clothes, Whirlpool says.

It has been revealed that say your jug’s label promises 64 loads at the medium-load line, and you’ve been pouring 50% more than that each time. The jug runs out after about 43 loads. Pour to the line and you get all 64 loads instead of 43, about 50% more, so two jugs now do the work of three.

Start with the fill line for your load size, using a high-efficiency (HE) detergent if your washer is an HE model. Then use less for a small or lightly soiled load or soft water, and more for a large or heavily soiled load or hard water (water high in minerals), as the institute advises.

The same goes for the bathroom shelf.

Before your next load, find the fill line your detergent’s label gives for the load you wash most, and pour to it every time.

#194040. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • Sources indicate that “Congratulations!
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun new way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which said something like,.

Sources indicate that “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

According to recent reports, okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

Industry observers note that so I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

But occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

It has been revealed that I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

Then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

But eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

Industry observers note that admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

According to recent reports, I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

According to recent reports, then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

It dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

In a recent development, it reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

It has been revealed that experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning newly introduced things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

Sources indicate that one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

Sources indicate that so I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

Sources indicate that thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

According to recent reports, so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

In a recent development, and of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

Recent findings suggest that as with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

We will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

Tech Report: Buy a Rental for Its Cash Flow – Treat Price Gains as a Bonus

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A rental that loses money each month is a bet that home prices will rise, and when they stall or fall, you keep covering the shortfall or sell at a loss.
  • Picture an investor who bought a condo in 2006 expecting price gains of 10% a year to make up for rent that fell $1,000 a month short of its costs.
  • Recent findings suggest that A rental with negative cash flow, meaning rent that falls short of its costs, pays off only if prices climb fast enough to cover the shortfall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rental that loses money each month is a bet that home prices will rise, and when they stall or fall, you keep covering the shortfall or sell at a loss. Buy one whose rent covers every cost, from the mortgage to repairs and vacancies, and treat any rise in value as extra.

Picture an investor who bought a condo in 2006 expecting price gains of 10% a year to make up for rent that fell $1,000 a month short of its costs. By 2011 the condo was worth 30% less, and the investor sold at a loss after paying $60,000 to cover five years of shortfalls.

Recent findings suggest that A rental with negative cash flow, meaning rent that falls short of its costs, pays off only if prices climb fast enough to cover the shortfall. Every repair and every vacancy adds to the shortfall, and borrowing makes a price drop worse. With 20% down, a 20% fall in price wipes out your whole down payment, because the loan doesn’t shrink when the price does.

The Federal Housing Finance Agency’s national index of home prices fell nearly 20% from its April 2007 peak by March 2011. In Austin, Texas, home prices jumped nearly 60% from 2020 to 2022, then the median price fell 22% from its pandemic peak by mid-2025, the Texas Real Estate Research Center found. Over the long run, most of what houses earned came from rent. In a typical year from 1890 to 2006, a house returned about 9% after inflation, with 7.7% from rent, before expenses, and only 1.3% from rising prices, a Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia working paper found.

It has been revealed that so buy only a property whose rent covers the mortgage, taxes, insurance, and a budget for repairs and vacancies. In an expensive market, that may mean buying in a city where rent still covers a mortgage. Run the full numbers before you make an offer. If the rent falls short, put more down to shrink the payment, or wait for a property that pays its own way.

Count the loan balance you pay down each month, and any rise in value, as your long-run gain, not as money toward the monthly costs.

You can hold a rental that covers its own costs through a slump, because the rent, not your paycheck, keeps paying the loan.

Skip Fabric Softener & Dryer Sheets – Most Loads Don’t Need Them

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stop buying fabric softener and dryer sheets by habit.
  • According to recent reports, A $13 jug of Downy covers 190 medium loads, and a $10 box of Bounce holds 240 sheets.
  • Both work by coating fibers so they feel smoother and cling less, and that coating is the catch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stop buying fabric softener and dryer sheets by habit. Softener can make towels less absorbent and leave a residue that traps odor in workout clothes, and most other laundry comes out fine without either. For static, dry your synthetic fabrics in their own load and take them out as soon as they’re dry.

According to recent reports, A $13 jug of Downy covers 190 medium loads, and a $10 box of Bounce holds 240 sheets. A family that washes the roughly 300 loads a year ENERGY STAR notes is average, using a medium dose and one sheet each time, spends about 11 cents a load, or about $33 a year.

Both work by coating fibers so they feel smoother and cling less, and that coating is the catch. Consumer Reports says liquid softener leaves a film that makes towels less absorbent and more flammable. Nike says softener leaves a residue on workout clothes that traps odor-causing bacteria and that sheets clog the fabric, so detergent has a harder time getting in. CHOICE, Australia’s consumer group, warns that softeners can also weaken the flame resistance of children’s sleepwear.

It has been revealed that so check the care label before reaching for softener, and keep it away from towels, workout clothes, kids’ pajamas, and anything labeled flame resistant. Softener changes how fabric feels, not how clean it gets, so the rest of the wash can skip it too.

In a recent development, for static, the fix costs nothing. Whirlpool, the appliance maker, says synthetics such as polyester and nylon are especially prone to static and that over-drying makes it worse. So dry them in a load of their own on low heat or the dryer’s moisture-sensing setting.

It has been revealed that wool dryer balls, sold as a reusable swap for sheets, start at about $9 for a set of six, roughly a quarter of the $33 a year that softener and sheets cost. Whirlpool says wool balls help prevent static by absorbing moisture. But a 2016 test by Consumer NZ found no less static and no softer clothes with dryer balls. CHOICE’s 2024 test found that none of the balls it tried did much for drying time or energy use. Treat them as optional.

Use up the jug and box you have, then leave both off the shopping list and keep about $33 a year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before you list a rental, write down the income, credit, landlord references, and eviction history an applicant needs. Then verify each one for every applicant instead of taking the application’s word for it. One written standard helps you pick tenants who pay and keeps your decisions within fair housing law.

Industry observers note that turning away the wrong applicant costs a little more time with the unit empty. Removing the wrong tenant can take a court case and months of lost rent.

Recent findings suggest that A standard set before you meet anyone keeps a good first impression from outweighing a bad rental history. Say an applicant charms you at the showing, but their last landlord reports two months of unpaid rent. A standard that asks for on-time rent at the last two rentals rules them out, and the unit goes to the next complete application.

The Fair Housing Act bars most landlords from turning anyone away because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or having children under 18. A standard applied the same way to everyone is your record of why you turned someone down. In many states and cities, source-of-income laws also bar refusing an applicant whose housing voucher pays part of the rent.

A workable standard covers four things.

It has been revealed that if you check criminal records, write down which convictions count and how far back you’ll look, within your state’s and city’s rules. Latest Jersey and New York City make most landlords wait to run a criminal check until they’ve offered the unit, pending its result, to an applicant who meets the rest of the standard.

Use one written application for everyone, and keep its fee within what your state allows.

Hand every applicant the standard in writing before you take a fee or run a check. Washington requires landlords to share their criteria, in writing or posted, before any screening, and elsewhere it spares an applicant who can’t qualify a wasted fee.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that picture this: you've just crossed the Atlantic on a long-haul award, touched down at London Heathrow, and now you need to get to Rome for the real adventure to begin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Business class hops across Europe for fewer points than most domestic economy awards.

Industry observers note that picture this: you've just crossed the Atlantic on a long-haul award, touched down at London Heathrow, and now you need to get to Rome for the real adventure to begin. Most travelers at this point resign themselves to a cramped economy seat on a budget carrier, dragging luggage through a secondary terminal. But you? You're walking into the Virgin Atlantic clubhouse, sipping a Bloody Mary, and then settling into a proper business class seat for the 2.5-hour hop to Fiumicino. That's the magic of this redemption. Here's the math that should make your jaw drop. A business class seat on a short-haul European flight — London Heathrow to Rome, London to Athens, London to virtually any major European city — routinely retails for **$1,000 to $3,000 in cash**. Airlines know that business travelers on these routes are often on corporate accounts and will pay whatever it costs. The leisure traveler simply doesn't book business class on a two-hour flight because it feels absurd. And that's exactly the pricing inefficiency the ChooseFI community learns to exploit. Virgin Atlantic's Flying Club prices these short-haul European business class seats at a flat **17,500 miles one-way**. At the low end of that $1,000–$3,000 cash range, you're already extracting **5.7 cents per point** — well above what most programs deliver. At the high end, when those seats spike to $3,000 on peak travel dates, you're looking at a staggering **17.1 cents per point**. For context, most travel rewards experts consider 1.5–2 cents per point a solid redemption. This one can deliver *ten times* that. What makes this feel particularly right for the FI mindset is the positioning angle. This isn't just a standalone splurge — it's the finishing move on a transatlantic trip you've already largely funded with points. You've landed in London. You need to get to your final European destination. Instead of paying $200 for a budget airline seat that charges extra for your carry-on, you drop 17,500 Virgin miles and arrive refreshed, fed, and ready. The opportunity cost of those miles is low; the experiential upgrade is enormous. This is what travel rewards done right looks like: not flying business class because you're wealthy, but because you understood the system better than the airlines expected you to.

The core insight here is understanding how Virgin Atlantic prices its own metal versus partner awards — and then deliberately choosing the right one for the right job.

In a recent development, virgin Atlantic's Flying Club is famous in the points community for two things. First, its partner award sweet spots: ANA First Class for as low as 55,000–60,000 miles one-way, Delta One at competitive rates. These are the headline acts. But quietly sitting in the same award chart is a genuinely underappreciated gem — Virgin's own short-haul European business class, priced at a flat 17,500 miles regardless of the specific route within that distance band.

Why does Virgin price it this way? Virgin Atlantic operates as a premium carrier and sets its award chart to reflect aspirational redemptions — the kind that make Flying Club membership feel worthwhile. For long-haul routes on their own metal, their pricing is competitive but not exceptional. For short-haul Europe, however, the fixed pricing creates an opportunity: a two-hour flight to Rome or Athens costs the same 17,500 miles as a cheaper, shorter hop, but those premium routes have cash prices that routinely spike into the thousands. The chart wasn't built to be a loophole — it's just that cash prices for short-haul business class in Europe are genuinely volatile and often extraordinary.

Marriage, a Baby, or a Second Income? Change Your W-4 Within Weeks

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (480 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Payroll withholds tax for the household your W-4 describes until you hand in a new one.
  • Every paycheck after the change is withheld at the old setting.
  • Each employer withholds based only on its own paycheck and what your W-4 tells it, such as your filing status and children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Payroll withholds tax for the household your W-4 describes until you hand in a new one. Within weeks of a wedding, a divorce, a new baby, a second job, or new side income, run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator. Give your employer the new W-4 it fills in while enough paychecks remain to spread the correction.

Every paycheck after the change is withheld at the old setting. The gap grows each payday, and the paydays left to close it shrink.

Each employer withholds based only on its own paycheck and what your W-4 tells it, such as your filing status and children. So a spouse’s pay, a second job, or side income on your return calls for more withholding. A divorce final by December 31 usually does too, since you’ll be taxed as unmarried for the whole year while payroll still withholds as married. A newly introduced child, or a spouse with no income, lets you have less withheld.

Run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator with your latest pay stub. It counts the new deductions for tips, overtime, seniors, and car loan interest, then fills in a new W-4 that payroll has about a month to start using. When a change like a divorce or a second job leaves you short for the year, the IRS requires the new form within 10 days.

Say newlyweds earn $60,000 each, are paid every two weeks, have no other income, and take the standard deduction. Both switch to married filing jointly in January and skip Step 2, the two-jobs step. Each employer gives its paycheck the couple’s whole standard deduction and lowest brackets, so by our math they end the year about $4,400 short. Fix it in July, and each spouse’s 13 remaining paychecks need about $170 more withheld apiece. Wait until October, and each spouse’s last six need about $360 apiece.

Side income from freelance or gig work has nothing withheld. Extra withholding in Step 4(c) can cover its tax, and when that’s more than your paychecks can spare, pay the rest in quarterly estimated payments. The IRS’s penalty rules count withholding as paid evenly through the year, so raising it in the fall also covers spring’s due dates, which a late estimated payment can’t.

Then rerun the estimator in late December, as the IRS advises, so a catch-up amount sized for a few paychecks doesn’t over-withhold all of next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that skin care results come from a short list of proven ingredients, like retinoids, vitamin C, and sunscreen, not from the price. Drugstore brands sell them, often for a fraction of luxury prices. Before you buy, check the label for the active ingredient and its strength, then pick the cheapest product that lists both.

A luxury retinol night cream that lists 0.3% retinol costs $160 an ounce. Drugstore night serums with the same 0.3% retinol cost $30 to $40 an ounce.

In a recent development, choosing a drugstore serum over the cream saves $120 to $130 an ounce, and the cream’s higher price doesn’t guarantee better results. The American Academy of Dermatology notes products that work come at every price, and its dermatologists rank sunscreen and moisturizer as the two most effective anti-aging buys.

Beyond those two, choose products by their active ingredient. In a 2025 study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology, dermatologists narrowed 318 skin care ingredients to 23 they agree on for problems like wrinkles, acne, and dark spots.

In a recent development, three of the 23 are drugstore staples. Match the one on the label to what you want to fix:.

It has been revealed that over-the-counter retinol products don’t have to state their strength on the label, so choose one that does and start with the lowest strength you can find. For any of the three, compare products by the ingredient and its strength, not the jar or the scent, and buy the cheapest one that matches. Makeup is a separate question, since how it looks on you is part of what you pay for.

Keep the daily routine to a cleanser, a moisturizer, and a sunscreen labeled broad-spectrum with SPF 30 or higher. A moisturizer with the same label counts as both. After a few weeks, add one active ingredient for the concern that bothers you most, since starting several at once can irritate your skin. Deep, painful acne or acne that scars needs a dermatologist from the start, because store-bought products are unlikely to clear it.

Give each new active ingredient at least six weeks, and if three months pass with no change, see a board-certified dermatologist instead of buying a pricier product.

The pink tax is the extra charged for a product marketed to women when it differs from the men’s version only in color, scent, or packaging. Compare the price per ounce or per item of both versions, check that the ingredients match, and buy the cheaper one, whichever aisle you find it in.

It has been revealed that when New York City’s Department of Consumer Affairs compared nearly 800 products sold in men’s and women’s versions in 2015, the women’s versions cost 7% more on average and 13% more for personal care. The widest gap was hair care, where women paid 48% more than men for shampoo and conditioner.

In a 2018 study of 10 personal care categories, the Government Accountability Office found women’s versions cost more in five, deodorant among them, but men’s cost more for shaving gel and nondisposable razors.

Some of the difference in the city’s study came from package size. It found men’s deodorant often sold in 2.7-ounce sticks and women’s in 2.6-ounce sticks at the same price, so compare the unit price, the cost per ounce or per item.

Recent findings suggest that say a pink four-pack of disposable razors costs $6 and the same razor in a blue six-pack costs $7.50. That’s $1.50 a razor against $1.25, so the blue pack is the cheaper buy. Then make sure the formulas match. For an antiperspirant, compare the active ingredient and strength on the Drug Facts label. For a shampoo, compare the first several ingredients, which are listed in order of amount.

In California and New York, a business can’t charge different prices for substantially similar products or services based on gender. A haircut or a dry-cleaning job can still cost more when it takes more time or skill. California’s Gender Tax Repeal Act also makes barbers, salons, tailors, and dry cleaners post prices for their standard services, and New York entitles you to a written price list on request from any service business.

Sources indicate that report a product priced by gender to California’s attorney general. In Upcoming York, file a complaint with the Division of Consumer Protection to seek back the difference you paid, or call its helpline at 1-800-697-1220.

Start with deodorant, the category both studies found pricier for women than for men, and compare the price per ounce of a men’s or unisex stick with the same active ingredient and strength.

Measure your pet’s meals with a kitchen scale or a level measuring cup, and feed the label’s amount for the weight your pet should be, not its current weight. Count treats as part of the day’s food. Eyeballed portions tend to run significant, so the bag empties sooner and the extra pounds raise vet bills.

In a recent development, those extra pounds are common. In the Association for Pet Obesity Prevention’s 2022 survey, veterinary professionals found 59% of dogs and 61% of cats overweight or obese.

Even a cup or scoop leaves room for error. When University of Guelph researchers had 100 dog owners measure set amounts of kibble, their portions ran from 48% too little to 152% too much, and the smallest amount, a quarter cup, gave them the most trouble.

In a recent development, say the feeding chart calls for a third of a cup a day and your cat gets half a cup. That’s 50% more than the chart’s amount, so a bag meant to last two months is gone in about six weeks and your cost per day rises by the same 50%. The American Animal Hospital Association’s nutrition guidelines link obesity to arthritis and diabetes. In Banfield Pet Hospital’s 2017 report, owners of overweight dogs spent 17% more on health care and 25% more on medications than owners of healthy-weight dogs.

According to recent reports, weigh meals on a kitchen scale, which the same guidelines rate as more accurate than measuring cups. Weigh one level cup of the food once, and a third-cup meal is a third of that weight. With a cup, pick one the size of the portion and level it off.

Use the chart’s amount for your pet’s ideal weight, which your vet can tell you, and treat it as a starting point. The guidelines base a pet’s calories on its ideal weight and warn that the amounts on labels can run high.

Keep treats to 10% of the day’s calories, the guidelines’ limit, or use pieces of the day’s measured kibble as treats. A bowl that stays full all day can’t be measured, so switch to set meals.

According to recent reports, then check your pet’s shape. You should be able to feel its ribs but not see them, and see a waist behind them from above. If you have to press to find the ribs, feed a little less, whatever the chart states.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that to give stock, transfer the shares to the recipient’s brokerage account or a child’s custodial account. Your cost basis, what you paid, goes with them, so the recipient owes tax on your gain when they sell. Give appreciated shares to someone whose low income means 0% tax on long-term gains, and sell losing shares yourself to deduct the loss.

The gain you built is then taxed at the recipient’s rate, not yours, so the right recipient can owe nothing.

Say shares you bought years ago for $2,000 are worth $10,000 now, and you pay 15% on long-term gains, those on investments held over a year. Selling them yourself costs $1,200 in federal tax on the $8,000 gain.

Give them to your daughter in her first full year of work after college. The time you’ve held them counts as hers, so she gets long-term rates at once. If her taxable income, the gain included, stays low enough for the 0% long-term rate, she owes no federal tax on it. The kiddie tax limits this for anyone under 18, and for 18-year-olds and full-time students under 24 whose earnings cover no more than half their support. It taxes their investment income above a small yearly amount at a parent’s rate when that’s higher.

Sources indicate that to make the gift, you’ll need the recipient’s brokerage name and account number for your broker’s online gift tool or form. For a child, open a custodial account, often called a UTMA or UGMA account, in their name. The shares become the child’s the day you give them, and the custodian manages them until the child comes of age.

In a recent development, giving over $19,000 in a year to one person other than your spouse means filing a gift tax return, but you owe tax only once your lifetime gifts pass a multimillion-dollar exemption. Shares given to a charity or a donor-advised fund leave no one owing tax on the gain, since charities pay no income tax. Heirs who inherit shares in a taxable account get the shares’ value at death as their basis, so the gain before then goes untaxed.

Never give shares worth less than you paid. Neither of you can deduct the drop that came before the gift. Sell them, deduct the loss on your own return, and give the cash.

Before the transfer, open your broker’s cost basis page and send only the batches of shares that have gained.

Sources indicate that the average electric dryer uses just over 690 kilowatt-hours of electricity a year, a field study the Northwest Energy Efficiency Alliance published in 2026 found. At the average U.S. residential rate of 18.16 cents per kilowatt-hour in August 2026, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, that comes to about $125 a year.

Industry observers note that the same study found the average household runs 307 full drying cycles a year, so each load costs about 40 cents to dry, and a load you hang costs nothing. A gas dryer costs less to run than an electric one, so hanging its loads saves less.

Recent findings suggest that at 40 cents a load, a couple who wash seven loads a week and hang five of them save $2 a week, or $104 a year, and cut their drying bill by more than 70%. Their $30 folding rack pays for itself in 15 weeks.

You don’t need a yard. A folding rack stands in a corner, a wall-mounted rack folds flat when it’s empty, and shirts dry on hangers hooked over the shower rod. A retractable line can stretch across a tub or a balcony, but check your lease or homeowners association’s rules for a ban on outdoor clotheslines before you hang one outside.

If you hang towels too, take them down while they’re still a little damp, then soften them with 10 minutes in the dryer. Air-drying also spares your clothes the dryer’s heat, which helps them last longer.

It has been revealed that for the loads you still dry, clean the lint screen every time and use the moisture-sensor or auto-dry setting instead of a timer, so the dryer stops once the clothes are dry. Run those loads back to back, too, while the drum still holds the last load’s heat.

Hang workout clothes and other lightweight synthetics first, since they dry faster than towels or jeans. At 40 cents a load, every weekly load you hang instead of drying saves about $21 a year.

The trail crosses eight states — Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, and Oregon — and stretches from Cape Girardeau on the banks of the Mississippi River to the small town of Port Orford on the edge of the Pacific Ocean.

Most of the route, roughly 70%, is unpaved. It is the organization’s longest off-road cycling trail, 1,120km longer than the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route.

It has been revealed that the Golden Gravel Trail route. Photo: The Adventure Cycling Association.

Stennes and Doyle finished in Cape Girardeau after 73 days, averaging an impressive 80km and around 12 hours of pedaling per day. “About 90% of it is mental,” they told Heartland News. “You might be tired, but you just keep on moving.”.

The couple are both experienced long-distance cyclists who have previously finished Montana’s Massive Sky Spectaculaire in six days and nine hours in 2022 (a self-supported 1,400km ultra-endurance race), among other bikepacking trips.

Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle during the 2022 Big Sky Spectaculaire. Photo: Bikepacking.com.

Recent findings suggest that likewise, the Adventure Cycling Association suggests riders should be self-supported for the Golden Gravel Trail. Riders are advised to carry two or three days’ worth of food for the route’s most isolated sections, and up to a day’s worth of water. This is particularly notable in the more arid sections, such as eastern Oregon. In Colorado, Utah, and Idaho, the trail traverses subranges of the Rockies and crosses the route’s highest point, Cumberland Pass at 3,668 m, in Colorado.

Stennes and Doyle say their journey included thunderstorms, aggressive farm dogs, and “countless hills.”.

My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

📅 16 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
  • But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
  • According to recent reports, I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

According to recent reports, I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

Recent findings suggest that but a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

It has been revealed that yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

One of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health tech giant that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

According to recent reports, long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

Another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

Sources indicate that so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s newly introduced organization, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

The next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

And wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

It’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

This is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

According to recent reports, it turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

In many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

But there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

In a recent development, many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

While this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

Sources indicate that distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

Recent findings suggest that and while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

It has been revealed that so I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

It has been revealed that I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty promptly in the past.

Recent findings suggest that but on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

Many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

Since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a fresh, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term looks again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

When you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that notes, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the matter, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

Recent findings suggest that the modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

It has been revealed that since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

Recent findings suggest that many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

More modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

My hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

In a recent development, and it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

Industry observers note that the great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The organization that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

Recent findings suggest that note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the washer’s motor is the cheap part of a load.
  • Take a standard washer, which uses about 20 gallons a load by Energy Star’s count, and assume a hot wash heats half of that, 10 gallons, from 50 to 120 degrees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that heating the water takes most of the energy your washing machine uses, so set everyday loads to cold and run the washer only when it’s full. Save hot water for the few loads that need it to kill germs or cut grease.

In a recent development, the washer’s motor is the cheap part of a load. Energy Star puts water heating at about 90% of a clothes washer’s energy use.

Take a standard washer, which uses about 20 gallons a load by Energy Star’s count, and assume a hot wash heats half of that, 10 gallons, from 50 to 120 degrees. With an electric water heater, that takes about 1.7 kilowatt-hours, roughly 30 cents at 17.23 cents per kilowatt-hour, the 2025 average residential price from the Energy Information Administration.

According to recent reports, A gas water heater that gets about 80% of its fuel’s heat into the water does the same job for about 11 cents, at the agency’s 2025 residential average of $15.34 per thousand cubic feet. Switching from hot to warm can cut either cost in half, Energy Star notes, and the cold cycle cuts the cost further. An Energy Star front-loader uses about half the water of a top-loader with an agitator, so switching it to cold saves less.

Hot water is still worth paying for on a few loads. During a stomach bug, the CDC notes to wash clothes, towels, or bedding with vomit or stool on them in hot water on the longest cycle, then machine dry them on the highest heat. Greasy work clothes are the other case, since Energy Star’s advice to wash cold makes an exception for oily stains. Wash everything else on cold, with a detergent made for cold water, as the South Carolina Energy Office advises.

According to recent reports, run fewer, fuller loads, too, and start them at night or on weekends if your utility charges less at those times. A washer uses about the same energy whatever the size of the load, Energy Star claims, so two half loads cost about twice what one full load does. If a small load can’t wait, set the water level to match it. For the rest of the electric bill, start with heating, cooling, and hot water.

A family that switches eight warm loads a week to cold saves up to $61 a year with an electric water heater, or $22 with gas.

Search teams have found the body of Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, of Germany, who went missing after he reached Camp 3 on his way down from the summit. Evidence shows he fell 1,700m to his death.

Industry observers note that waschiczek was one among over 200 climbers who lined up toward the summit of Ama Dablam this past weekend. He reached the top on October 25 with guide Sonam Sherpa, but for some reason the two of them stopped descending at a rather high point on the mountain.

“The pair decided to stay at Camp 3 overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” his expedition outfitter, Real Himalaya Nepal, told The Tourism Times.

It has been revealed that climbers above Camp 3 on Ama Dablam. Photo: Dorjee Gyalzen Sherpa.

According to recent reports, according to the outfitter, the climbers prepared to continue down this morning. Lama asked his client to stay in place while he returned the sleeping bag to the tent where he had borrowed it. When the Sherpa returned, Waschiczek was nowhere to be found, but his crampons were still there, which suggested a freak fall. A search helicopter was called, and the remains of the climber were found this afternoon at around 4,500m.

Waschiczek is the first fatality on Ama Dablam this season.

Together with Manaslu, Ama Dablam is the most popular fall mountain in Nepal. The latest enhancement from Nepal’s Department of Tourism on October 17 demonstrated that over 300 foreign climbers had applied for a climbing permit. That day, the rope-fixing team opened the route to the top, and a massive summit wave started a couple of days later.

According to recent reports, virtually all foreign climbers are guided by one or two Sherpas, so the summit rates and numbers are remarkable. Local media estimate that over 200 climbers, among locals and foreigners, have topped out so far this season. Further teams should join them over the rest of October and November. However, no matter how tamed with ropes and anchors Ama Dablam gets, a fall from its steep slopes is usually lethal.

The upper part of Ama Dablam at sunset. Photo: 8K Expeditions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for the second time in just over a month, a violent storm is approaching Nepal and threatening two meters of fresh snow on already overloaded mountains. This newly introduced setback comes at the height of the trekking season and also affects several climbing teams, including those engaged in alpine-style expeditions in remote areas.

The first storm hit Nepal toward the end of September and abruptly ended the climbing season on Manaslu. Worst of all, it caused an avalanche that killed 16 Base Camp staff on Himlung. The mountain remained open to commercial expeditions despite the accident, and several guided teams are right now launching their summit pushes.

Manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal. Photo: Shiddi Ghising.

A low-pressure front that formed in the Bay of Bengal has now developed into a deep depression and will turn into a full cyclone tomorrow. It is expected to hit Nepal on Wednesday or Thursday through the end of the week.

It has been revealed that the Nepal National Mountain Guides Association, in association with Senior Meteorologist Krishna Bhakta Manandhar, has put out a detailed forecast. They note that clouds spreading out from this system will hit Nepal’s mountains on October 28, especially above 6,500-7,000m in the eastern part of Nepal, including the Khumbu and Kanchenjunga regions. This will spread over the next two days, causing heavy rains throughout Nepal and snow at higher altitudes.

Authorities and local media have urged trekkers and climbers to modify their plans and avoid river areas and high passes. The main concern is for those currently in remote areas without InReach, Starlink, or satphones.

Recent findings suggest that trekkers should check with local agencies, especially those heading for the Annapurna and Manaslu regions. Several passes there were already cut or in poor condition after the previous storm and subsequent floods.

A Russian team in the Kangchenjunga region is acclimatizing to climb 7,710m Jannu. According to their latest report, they initiative to touch 7,000m before attempting their main goal.

It has been revealed that fellow Russians attempting the West Ridge of Everest have retreated to Kathmandu to rest and recover, so they should not be affected. Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov, all climbing without supplemental oxygen, are enduring some lung problems. They returned to Base Camp from their second foray up the mountain last Friday, without reaching 7,500m, as they’d hoped.

It has been revealed that after climbing in the Cholu range, Jost Kobusch of Germany and his small team moved to the Manaslu area for the second stage of his acclimatization before attempting Everest solo in winter, also without oxygen and via the West Ridge. However, the poor state of the trails after the recent floods and the approaching cyclone have thwarted his prepares.

“The flood cut our planned path and, according to forecasts, the incoming cyclone will leave up to two meters of snow,” Kobusch told ExplorersWeb from Samagaon, where the team is pondering their options.

Night and evening work lets you earn extra money without giving up your days, from overnight stocking, security, and caregiving shifts to delivery and tutoring gigs you schedule yourself. Before you take an employer’s night shift, ask whether it pays a shift differential, a premium for night hours, since the federal minimum wage and overtime law doesn’t require one.

These hours suit night owls, students with daytime classes, parents who trade shifts with a partner, and anyone adding paid hours after a day job.

Industry observers note that the Department of Labor says extra pay for night work is a matter for you and the employer to agree on, or for a union that represents you. The federal government, for one, adds 10% to the basic pay of employees on its General Schedule pay scale for regularly scheduled work between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m., the Office of Personnel Management says.

The pay below is each job’s median hourly wage for May 2025 from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, tips included. Those medians leave out shift differentials, so a night premium would come on top. If a store pays its overnight stockers $2 an hour more than its day crew, 30 hours of night work a week bring in $60 more than the same hours by day.

These pay by the trip, the order, or the tutoring hour, and you choose when to log on. The driving numbers come from Gridwise, an app drivers use to track their earnings, for the third quarter of 2026, and they’re gross pay, before your gas, car wear, and taxes. Work out your hourly pay after costs before you count on one.

If the night job will be your second one, adjust the tax withheld from your paychecks and check your main employer’s rules on taking a second job before the first shift.

Sources indicate that A night premium can cover only part of a shift, the way the federal one counts only hours between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. Before you accept an employer’s night shift, ask what it pays per hour at night and which hours earn that rate.
