#194017. Mont Blanc Has Grown Almost Two Meters — But Not in the Way You Think

📅 27 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (554 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

Mont Blanc Has Grown Almost Two Meters — But Not in the Way You Think

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • These days, topographic surveys typically show that a mountain’s altitude is decreasing due to shrinking snowcaps.
  • It has been revealed that mont Blanc is now 1.88 meters taller than it was three years ago, according to a recent report by France’s IGN (National Geographic Institute).
  • However, it may be wise to wait before changing the figure in climbing guides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These days, topographic surveys typically show that a mountain’s altitude is decreasing due to shrinking snowcaps. But strangely, Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, has grown significantly since its latest measurement in 2023.

It has been revealed that mont Blanc is now 1.88 meters taller than it was three years ago, according to a recent report by France’s IGN (National Geographic Institute). The new official altitude is now 4,807.47 meters (15,772.5 feet) above sea level.

However, it may be wise to wait before changing the figure in climbing guides. Measurements are carried out every two years, and each time the registered altitude varies:.

Graphic showing the results of the last few measurements on Mont Blanc, by LaChangingMeteo.

Mont Blanc’s “summit is constantly shifting,” Jean des Garets, chief geometer in the Haute-Savoie department, told Le Monde. “Each individual measurement is not significant in itself.”.

Industry observers note that so, what’s with the yearly differences? Obviously, it’s the variation in the thick but ever-changing snowcap that covers the summit.

Sources indicate that the mountain’s rocky summit measures around 4,792m above sea level. The snow cover varies with the seasons. The difference from the previous measurement shows that 2023 was much drier at summit altitude.

The survey team on itsir way to the summit of Mont Blanc.. Photo: ING.

It has been revealed that A team from the Order of Chartered Surveyors (Ordre des géomètres-experts) acclimatized first by climbing Bishorn (4,153m). They then spent some days measuring several points around the mountain. Finally, they climbed Mont Blanc via the normal route on September 15-16.

Once on top, they pinpointed the highest point using a GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) pole, which measures altitude in real time.

The recent survey featured an interesting novelty. In addition to altitude, the survey also measured Mont Blanc’s gravity by installing a gravimeter on the summit for the first time ever. This measured the force with which the Earth attracts the device. In so doing, they wanted to determine whether the summit has sunk, regardless of ice cover.

The gravimeter on the summit of Mont Blanc, September 16. Photo: ING France.

“When the height of Mont Blanc changes, we can’t know for sure whether the ground or the rock has moved or if the ice has melted,” explains Olivier Jamet.

In a recent development, gravity provides the missing information: mass. If the ice has melted, there is less material under the instrument, but the rock has moved closer to it. Distinguishing these two effects requires a model of the ice cap and the massif, and above all, repeated measurements at the same location. And the effort is worthwhile, especially now that the effects of climate change on Alpine glaciers are becoming increasingly apparent.

The gravimeter on the top of Mont Blanc measured the gravity at 9.7944689 m/s².

“For comparison, this value is 9.81 m/s² in Marseille (located at sea level) and 9.8043046 m/s² in Saint-Gervais-Le Fayet (580m above sea level),” ING reports. “This difference in value, even if it seems small, allows for the detection of changes in mass, particularly in the mass of the ice. Repeated over time, these gravity measurements will thus contribute to improving the determination of the altitude of the highest peak in Western Europe.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in April, Robert Cowden, 52, set off on foot from New Haven, Kansas, on a two-stage journey across the United States. First, he planned to walk nearly 2,000km to Pittsburgh, then canoe 3,200km downriver to the Gulf of Mexico. With him is his dog, Enzo, a pointer-mix.

It has been revealed that robert Cowden and Enzo. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

Sources indicate that when he left New Haven with Enzo, Cowden was at a low point. His battle with alcohol addiction had cost him his job, car, and home. Entering a residential treatment program would leave Enzo with no place to go. Now sober and with housing waiting for him after the end of his journey, Cowden sees his expedition as part of the larger effort to rebuild his life.

According to recent reports, during the walking stage, Cowden towed his camping gear and supplies in a cart, which Enzo could ride in to take a break from walking. Setting out with very little, Cowden has relied on the kindness of strangers, both online and on the trail, to continue his expedition.

“The number one warning you’re going to get on a walk across America is, ‘Be careful, there’s creepy people and bad people,'” Cowden recalled, speaking to a local KOMU 8 reporter while passing through Missouri. Instead, he’s been overwhelmingly met with generosity and helpfulness.

Cowden shows the wear on his trail shoes, as Enzo looks on. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

It has been revealed that cowden completed the walking stage in September. Now, he’s on the Ohio River and hopes to reach the Gulf by the end of 2026. While the second stage lets him and Enzo get off their feet, it has its own challenges. They debuted the canoe into the Allegheny River at Pittsburgh. It soon joined the Ohio, and lengthy stretches of slow water pushed Cowden to paddle continuously.

Sources indicate that it’s 1,579km down the Ohio to its confluence with the Mississippi in Illinois, which Cowden and Enzo aim to complete in under 40 days. They’re presently on pace, averaging about 20km a day.

Cowden posts regular updates on Facebook and on the expedition’s webpage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pay high-end prices only for makeup you wear on your whole face every day, which mostly means foundation, and test it with a free sample before you buy. Start with drugstore mascara, eyeliner, and lip color, since manufacturers usually recommend replacing mascara every few months, whatever you paid for it.

According to recent reports, A department-store brand and a drugstore brand can belong to the same tech giant. L’Oréal, which owns both Lancôme and Maybelline Fresh York, spent 32.2% of its 2025 sales on advertising and promotion, about 10 times what went to research and innovation.

In a recent development, so a higher price doesn’t prove a better formula. Pay more only where the difference indicates every day and you’ll use the product long enough to get your money’s worth.

It has been revealed that foundation qualifies. It covers your whole face every day, so a shade that’s slightly off is easy to spot, and it usually stays usable longer than eye makeup. The FDA notes that eye-area products tend to go bad faster than other cosmetics, and that manufacturers usually recommend throwing mascara out two to four months after purchase.

That makes mascara the easiest place to save, because you pay any premium again with every new tube. At one tube every three months, a $30 department-store mascara costs $120 a year, against $48 for a $12 drugstore tube. The gap is $72 a year on one product.

Sources indicate that try drugstore eyeliner and lip color first too, and buy them where one that disappoints can go back. Ulta Beauty, which stocks drugstore brands, refunds most new or gently used products returned within 30 days of purchase, so keep the receipt.

It has been revealed that for foundation, test before you pay. Sephora stores offer a free shade match with a skin-tone scanner, and you can ask a Beauty Advisor for a free sample of any brand in any shade. Look up dupes too, cheaper products that closely match a pricier one, and read reviews that compare the two side by side.

Wear the sample through a full day and check it in daylight, then buy the bottle only if it still matches.

#194012. Industry News: Financing Your First Rental? Expect 15% to 25% Down and a Higher Rate

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (507 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Financing Your First Rental? Expect 15% to 25% Down and a Higher Rate

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finance a rental property with a conventional investment mortgage when your income qualifies, or a DSCR loan, which looks at the rent instead, when it doesn’t.
  • Lenders charge more on a home you won’t live in because the loan is riskier for them.
  • If your income qualifies, start with a conventional investment mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finance a rental property with a conventional investment mortgage when your income qualifies, or a DSCR loan, which looks at the rent instead, when it doesn’t. Either way, plan on 15% to 25% down, a rate at least half a percentage point above a home loan’s, and several months of payments in savings. Get preapproved before you make offers.

Lenders charge more on a home you won’t live in because the loan is riskier for them.

If your income qualifies, start with a conventional investment mortgage. Under Freddie Mac rules, it takes 25% down on a building with two to four units and as little as 15% on a single-family rental. Below 20% down, you’ll also pay for mortgage insurance. A duplex you’ll live in counts as your home instead and can take 5% down.

A DSCR loan, short for debt service coverage ratio, qualifies you on how well the property’s rent covers its payment instead of on your income. It usually costs more than a conventional loan, so it’s the fallback when your income won’t qualify, and DSCR lenders often want a credit score of at least 680 and 20% to 25% down. Some banks also make portfolio loans, which they keep rather than sell, so they set their own terms.

According to recent reports, on a conventional loan, Fannie Mae’s reserve rule asks for six months of the rental’s full payment, taxes and insurance included, in savings, investments, or vested retirement money. Its rental income rule counts 75% of the expected rent, and if you’ve managed rentals for less than a year, that rent can only cover the property’s own payment, never count as income.

In a recent development, borrowing the down payment against your own house, with a home equity line of credit, puts the house at risk unless your paycheck can repay the line. Telling a lender you’ll live in a home you proposal to rent is what the Federal Housing Finance Agency calls occupancy fraud.

Say you buy a $250,000 rental with 25% down and a 30-year fixed loan at 7.75%, against 7% on a home loan. You’d bring $62,500 plus closing costs and six months of payments in reserve, and pay about $1,343 a month in principal and interest, $96 more than the same loan’s $1,247 at 7%.

Get preapproved by two or three lenders, one of them a local bank or credit union, for the loan you’ll use before you make an offer.

To find lenders for those preapprovals, compare the best mortgage lenders.

#194011. U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

📅 28 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1115 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1115 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).
  • In a recent development, the team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style.
  • In a recent development, on the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).

In a recent development, the team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style. They summited on October 20 and rode/skied down via the same line on the south face, while American photographer Blake Gordon and Canadian cinematographer Leo Hoorn filmed from a high camp.

In a recent development, on the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026. Photo: Nick Russell.

“The south face of Dorje was always the goal, and I’d been planning/dreaming of it for over two years,” Nick Russell told ExplorersWeb while on his way to the airport.

The expedition reached base camp on October 6, shortly after an intense storm blanketed Nepal’s mountains with heavy snow. For them, however, the snow was a blessing rather than a curse.

“The cyclone gave our zone some much-needed snow down low, and on the face, it allowed a clean descent (no down climbing, no rappels),” Russell noted.

Recent findings suggest that sickness slowed the beginning of the expedition. “Three out of five of us, myself included, caught COVID,” Russell said. Luckily, the climbers recovered just as the weather cleared and winds dropped, followed by a string of perfect days.

According to recent reports, after the descent. Photo: Nick Russell/Instgram.

“Adam, Billy, and I all carried our own gear, set the tracks, and climbed in alpine style on the face,” Nick Russell noted. The team had hired three Sherpa climbers (Dawa Geljee Sherpa, Kami Sherpa, and Nuri Sherpa) who helped the camera crew get their gear to a high camp, plus a base camp crew, outfitted by Shangri-La Nepal Trek.

In a recent development, high camp at 6,000m on the south face of Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

The line of ascent/descent followed the snow from below 4,500m to Camp 1 (4,900m) by crossing an icefall. According to the team, this was the only real crux of the ascent, due to overhead serac hazard. At least, the exposed section was short — less than an hour.

According to recent reports, on the first day of the summit push, the team continued to their high camp at 6,000m, below the col and at the base of the snowy face. Russell recalls the details of the climb as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that the south face is quite steep and sustained above the bergshrund, with sustained 45-50˚ and pockets of 55º, we estimate. The face had seen so much sun [over] the past two weeks that the rising conditions were the biggest unknown of the entire project.

We didn’t know whether or not it would be too icy to ride/ski until we got on the face. The snow was mostly firm, pretty much on the brink of being edge-able. It was two tool and crampon climbing the entire way, with no proper rests to take the pack off.

In a recent development, it took about 7.5 hours to climb the face, and we topped out around 1:30 pm. It took roughly 1.5 hours to descend, with breaks for the cameras to reset.

A climber leaves almost no tracks in the hard snow on Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

The three summiters started down from the top at the same time, Russell on snowboard and his partners on skis. It was anything but easy.

Industry observers note that “The snow was more firm than I would have liked, but just edgeable enough to hold an edge,” Russell recalls. “Between the altitude, exposure below, steepness, and how firm it was, it was by far the heaviest line I’ve ever ridden.” He added that if the snow had been a little harder, they would have had to rappel down.

Recent findings suggest that the hard snow on the upper sections. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

“You always hope for stable, boot-top powder, but that’s rarely the case at high altitude,” Russell explained. “Instead, you make the most of the conditions presented and try to do it as safely as possible.”.

Recent findings suggest that he added: “The entire line was a no-fall zone; one lost edge, and it’d be over. Regardless of conditions, it was a dream for all of us to ride off the top of a peak in Nepal.”.

After a partial descent, the team spent the night at high camp, hoping to ride some interesting slopes they had spotted earlier, but finally decided to bail the next morning. “We were satisfied,” Russell said. They continued on skis/snowboard all the way down to the moraines below Camp 1 around 4,500m.

Recent findings suggest that childhood friends Fabrikant and Haas often partner up on major ski expeditions, mainly in Alaska but also in the Himalaya. They climbed and skied both Gasherbrums 1 and 2 without oxygen after climbing them in the same style in 2024, together with Brendan O’Neill.

“They are the strongest partners I’ve ever been in the mountains with,” noted Russell, who has also climbed and snowboarded twice in the Indian Himalaya and twice in Nepal.

“I tried Dhaulagiri in 2022 with Blake Gordon and Dan Corn, but the difficult conditions that year coupled with the loss of Hilaree Nelson [who fell to her death while trying to ski down Manaslu] didn’t allow us to make very much progress,” Russell said.

“I’ve always dreamed of riding lines in the Himalaya, and this felt like a major step forward in my personal journey,” he concluded.

While this is the first ski and snowboard descent of Dorje Lhakpa’s south face, the legendary Marco Siffredi snowboarded the west ridge of the mountain in 1999, with Bertrand Delapierre. Siffredi perished shortly afterward on the Hornbein Couloir on Mount Everest. “Dorje Lhakpa first entered my psyche from Marco and Bertrand’s descent,” the rider recalled.

The south face of Dorje Lhakpa was only climbed for the first time in 2021, by Spaniards Mikel Inoriza, Iker Madoz, and Mikel Zabalza.

“I came across a photo of the south face and the American Alpine Journal article from the Spanish team’s first ascent in 2021,” Russell said. “The massive south face is visible from the Kathmandu Valley on a clear day, and it is honestly crazy to me that no one had skied it before.”.

In a recent development, “Today,” he went on, “people are so hyper-focused on the 8,000m peaks (for good reason, I get it), but there are still virgin lines waiting for a snowboard/ski descent in the 6,000-7,000m range. It just takes a shit ton of work to make it happen.”.

  • The buyer signs a promissory note, an IOU setting the rate, the term, and any balloon, the lump sum due at the end.

Offer seller financing on your house only if it’s paid off or your mortgage lender agrees in writing. You become the buyer’s lender, so protect yourself the way a bank would, with a credit and income check, at least 10% down, a real estate attorney to draft the note, and a loan servicing company to collect it.

According to recent reports, lending to the buyer opens your house to people a bank won’t approve, which can sell it faster or for more, and pays you interest. It also leaves you with the lender’s risk that the payments stop.

The buyer signs a promissory note, an IOU setting the rate, the term, and any balloon, the lump sum due at the end. A mortgage or deed of trust recorded in your favor gives you the right to foreclose if they default.

Federal rules for loan originators, the professionals who arrange mortgages, don’t apply to a homeowner who finances only one sale in any 12-month period. A balloon doesn’t change that, as long as the payments never let the balance grow and the rate is fixed, or adjusts only after five years, on the rules’ terms. If you still owe on the house, check your mortgage for a due-on-sale clause, which lets the lender demand the full balance if you sell without first getting its written consent.

Before you close, put these protections in place.

In a recent development, say you sell a paid-off $250,000 house with $25,000 down and finance the other $225,000 at 7%, with payments set as if the loan ran 30 years and the balance due after five. You’d collect about $1,497 a month, then about $212,000 when the buyer refinances to pay the balloon.

Until then, most of your sale price stays tied up in the loan. The interest is taxable income, and any taxable profit on the sale can be reported as the payments arrive. Offer financing only with money you won’t need until the note is paid off.

Sources indicate that what you spend on drinking comes in small charges that are easy to miss: bar tabs, bottles for home, tips, delivery fees, and rides home. Add up a month of them, then try a month without alcohol, set a weekly spending limit after it, and move the difference into savings.

The average household spent $630 on alcohol in 2025, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports, and that figure includes households that don’t drink at all.

It has been revealed that say a couple spends $90 a week on drinks out and $30 on bottles for home. That’s $480 every four weeks and $6,240 a year, nearly 10 times the $630 average, before counting any rides home.

To find your own number, go through last month’s card and bank statements. Add up every bar tab with its tip, every bottle bought for home, every alcohol delivery and its fees, and every ride home from a night out, plus any cash you spent at bars. Multiply that total by 12 to see what drinking costs you in a year.

In a recent development, then go a month without drinking. Use Dry January or any month with no wedding, vacation, or major birthday on the calendar. Each week, move what you would have spent, about a quarter of last month’s total, into a high-yield savings account. The couple above would have $480 put away after four weeks. If going without is harder than you expected, call SAMHSA’s National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. The federal line is free, confidential, and open 24/7, and it refers callers to local treatment, support groups, and community organizations.

Once the month is over, a few habits keep the cost down without cutting the ride home. Swap some bar nights for a potluck at home or other cheap things to do with friends, alternate each drink with a glass of water, and go out at happy hour, when drinks cost less.

Set a weekly limit on what you spend on drinks, and keep moving the difference between that limit and your old weekly spending into savings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S. from Canada to Mexico. Starting in Glacier National Park, they will cross four rivers and six U.S. states to finish in El Paso, Texas.

Their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails. This allows the pair to cross landscapes that would usually require separate trips by bike and watercraft. Streufert, a geospatial wildfire scientist and cartographer, came up with the route by combining existing GPS tracks and geographical data from Bikepacking.com, American Whitewater, and OpenStreetMap. He overlaid cycling corridors and rivers to identify where the two could connect.

According to recent reports, before starting the journey on September 17, he mentioned they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes. So it is possible that they are the first to do so.

Sources indicate that they started what they neatly call the Saddle to Paddle Traverse on September 17, from Glacier National Park, Montana, on the Canadian border. They kicked off the first packrafting section with a 115km descent of the North Fork of the Flathead River, which forms part of the western boundary of Glacier National Park.

Recent findings suggest that from there, they followed the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route through Montana toward Jackson Lake, Wyoming, for 1,107km. Here, they hit their second paddling phase on the Snake River.

Every time they reach a river, the pair inflates their rafts, load their bicycles aboard, and paddle downstream. Then at each takeout, they deflate the rafts, attach them to their bikes, and continue riding.

Sources indicate that the route. Photo: Pete Streufert.

In a recent development, after 130km along the Snake River, their route joined the SLoToJa cycling corridor. They pedaled through Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Here, a short connector track took them onto the newly developed Golden Gravel Trail. A further 860km of cycling brought them to Utah’s Green River.

They then paddled 328km through Desolation and Gray Canyons, including a handful of Class III rapids, and their only Class IV rapid of the trip.

Pulling their rafts out in Canyonlands National Park, they took the White Rim Trail to Moab. They are now taking a few days in Moab to “get all the mud off our bikes and escape the rain for a day or two before we keep heading south,” states Streufert.

From here, they will once again pick up the Golden Gravel Trail through the La Sal Mountains and across Colorado, then continue on the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route to New Mexico.

Paddling the Green River. Photo: Pete Streufert.

A final paddling section on Upcoming Mexico’s Rio Chama will take them to the last leg of the trip, a 950km ride to El Paso.

According to recent reports, the pair are riding Rodeo Labs Flaanimal 6.0 Steel, fitted with 29-inch Vittoria Mezcal tires, and using Kokopelli packrafts. The pair have described this as a “self-supported” route, although of course they’re replenishing their food along the way. They seem to combine camping with staying in towns.

View this post on Instagram See this post on Instagram.

They should complete the journey within the next few weeks, within their two-month timeline. You can follow their progress here.

  • To see whether anyone fits, list everyone who would lose income or pick up a bill if you died next month, and how many years each would need help.
  • Industry observers note that the obvious names are a spouse and young kids, plus anyone who shares a debt with you, such as a partner on the mortgage or a parent who co-signed a loan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You need life insurance if your death would leave someone short of money, such as a spouse or kids living on your income, a partner on your mortgage, or a co-signer. If no one fits, skip it. If someone does, buy a term policy, which covers a set number of years, while you’re young and the price is low.

To see whether anyone fits, list everyone who would lose income or pick up a bill if you died next month, and how many years each would need help.

Industry observers note that the obvious names are a spouse and young kids, plus anyone who shares a debt with you, such as a partner on the mortgage or a parent who co-signed a loan. Easier to miss are a business partner who would need cash to buy your share of the business from your family, a parent whose rent you cover, and a child with a disability who will need support as an adult. A stay-at-home parent needs coverage too, since the family would have to pay someone for the childcare and housework.

If no one makes your list, you can skip the policy, provided your savings would pay for your funeral. Debts in your name alone don’t change that. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau states only your estate, the money and property you leave, owes them, though some state laws make a surviving spouse pay certain debts.

According to recent reports, if your list has names, check whether your employer’s coverage is enough before you count on it. Then work out how much the people on your list would need, and buy your own policy soon.

In a recent development, most buyers choose level term, the Insurance Information Institute notes. Your age and health when the policy starts set its premium, the price you pay, and that price stays the same for the whole term. Say a 30-year-old man who doesn’t smoke shares a $300,000, 30-year mortgage with his partner. A $300,000 policy that lasts 30 years would let his partner keep the house, and Ethos, which sells life insurance online, estimates it would cost $24 to $45 a month for a man that age in average health.

Buy coverage that lasts as long as the longest need on your list, such as a 30-year term policy for a latest 30-year mortgage, or one that runs until your youngest child finishes college.

Get quotes for that length from the best term life insurance companies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu. He is recovering in intensive care. By law, all foreign trekkers are supposed to have a guide in the Khumbu.

Sources indicate that joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass. He was first taken to Lobuche, then flown out on October 27, according to The Tourism Times.

Kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit. It links the Chhukung side of the Imja Valley with Lobuche over rocky, non-glaciated moraine. The crossing is long and remote; the descent toward Lobuche is often loose underfoot and comes after hours already spent at altitude.

Sources indicate that the case has again drawn attention to Nepal’s rules in the Khumbu. Since 2023, the Nepal Tourism Board has required that all foreign trekkers be accompanied by a licensed guide within national parks, including Sagarmatha.

In practice, the local Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality has continued to glitch its own permits and has not strictly enforced the national guide requirement. Thus, independent trekking remains common on the main Everest routes. Officials quoted by The Tourism Times described unguided travel in the region as a violation of the mandatory rule and a source of preventable rescues.

According to recent reports, cherubino was traveling alone when he was found. No further details on the circumstances of the fall or his condition have been released beyond the hospital’s assessment that he is recovering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every bet in a sports betting app carries a cut for the sportsbook, so the longer you bet, the likelier you are to end up behind. Treat betting as entertainment you pay for. Set what you can afford to lose each month as the app’s deposit limit before you start, and stop when it’s gone.

Winning half your bets sounds like breaking even. In a sports betting app, it loses money.

Industry observers note that the usual price on a point spread (a bet on a game’s margin of victory) is -110, which means you risk $110 to win $100. You have to win 52.4% of those bets just to break even. Say you bet $50 on each of 20 games a month at -110 and win exactly half. Your 10 wins bring in about $455 and your 10 losses cost $500, so you’re down about $45 a month, or about $545 a year. A broad stock fund held for years is expected to grow instead, which is why investing isn’t gambling.

According to recent reports, A parlay, one bet that pays only if all its picks win, costs more than a single bet, because the cut applies to each pick. With four picks at -110, each a 50% chance, the parlay pays about 12 to 1, though the odds against all four winning are 15 to 1. On average, the sportsbook keeps about 17 cents of every dollar on that parlay, versus about 4.5 cents on any one of those picks bet alone. Promos have catches too. Some make you bet your own money first, and a refund on a losing bet often comes only as credit to bet again on the same app, Michigan’s attorney general warns.

Set up the account so the limit holds:.

If you catch yourself betting more to win back losses or can’t cut back without feeling restless, call or text the National Problem Gambling Helpline at 1-800-MY-RESET (1-800-697-3738). It’s free to call and open 24/7.

  • Industry observers note that andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening.
  • In a recent development, everest West Ridge some days ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time. While no easy option exists, they want to avoid the extremely exposed, difficult, and uncertain ridge route. Their only alternative is the Hornbein Couloir, which would force them to stray temporarily into Tibet.

Industry observers note that andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening. They will return to their base in Lobuche this weekend, determined to climb Everest without supplemental oxygen.

In a recent development, everest West Ridge some days ago. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

“So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb. “Part of this time was spent exploring different options for accessing the route.”.

According to recent reports, the Russian team has a permit to climb Everest from Nepal, as long as they attempt a route other than the standard Khumbu Icefall-South Col-Southeast Ridge. This has become the normal South Side route since Hillary and Tenzing’s first ascent in 1953.

Topo of the Russian team’s planned route on Everest, courtesy of Andrei Vasiliev.

Recent findings suggest that first, the Russians tried to bypass the Khumbu Icefall via the Nuptse Shoulder toward Camp 1, but heavy snow forced them to find another route. Crossing the Icefall (sharing paths with the normal route) was also too hard in the deep snow and on the shaky snow bridges over the innumerable crevasses.

“Eventually, we selected a third option, via the Lho La,” Vasiliev remarked. “From that pass, our planned route continues across the West Shoulder, along the West Ridge.”.

Industry observers note that at the Lho La col. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Industry observers note that on their latest foray, the team reached 6,400m. “We climbed approximately twelve 60m pitches over rock, snow, and ice of moderate difficulty,” remarked Vasiliev.

He noted that on the way to the West Shoulder, they found traces of previous expeditions, including old ropes and snow anchors.

As for the terrain ahead of them, Vasiliev said:.

Recent findings suggest that from our highest point reached, the terrain ahead looks manageable. We can see two more steep rock steps, each approximately 100m high, along with possible bypasses on steep snow slopes. Beyond these obstacles, the terrain appears easier, and we hope to be able to move simultaneously.

Sources indicate that rocky section on the way to Everest’s West Ridge. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Vasiliev and his team are confident they can manage this route, despite doing so in increasingly wintry conditions.

The route linking the Lho La, the West Shoulder, and the West Ridge of Everest has been completed only twice. A Yugoslavian team led by Tone Skarja did the first complete ascent in 1979. They used the Hornbein Couloir variation on their descent.

In a recent development, the only repetition was done by a Bulgarian team in 1984. Hristo Prodanov reached the summit on his own and retraced his steps down the ridge but never made it back alive. Some of his partners who summited days later descended via the normal route. Three other teams who climbed the West Shoulder-West Ridge summited by traversing to the North Face, on the Chinese side, and climbing the Hornbein Couloir.

Industry observers note that the North Face of Everest from the West Shoulder. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Objectively speaking, the Hornbein Couloir offers more summit (and survival) chances than the upper part of the West Ridge. However, it requires traversing into Chinese territory. The Russian team has a permit to climb only from Nepal. It is unclear if a brief border trespass could be considered, and Vasiliev has not confirmed what they will do. “First we need to complete one more rotation,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that choose pieces that convert, like a crib that becomes a toddler bed, and skip single-purpose gadgets such as a wipe warmer. Sources indicate that since 1975, Nikon’s Small World competition has featured images produced by optical microscopes, an art that usually stays in scientific papers and textbooks. But through the carefully engineered lenses of the microscope, photomicrographers sometimes capture glimpses of strikingly surreal, alien beauty. The 2026 Photomicrography Competition winners include subjects both living and mechanical, small and very small.

In a recent development, the fruiting bodies of a Hemitrichia slime mold remind one distinctly of Dr. Seuss. Photo: Eric Epstein/Nikon Small World.

It has been revealed that the winning image shows bubbling globules of black ink being injected onto a piece of paper by an inkjet printer. Behind the lens was 25-year-old German design student Ole Bielfeldt, whose work explores the surprising complexity of everyday objects. His process is largely DIY: Bielfeldt builds his own setups, cobbles together parts, and learns techniques online.

It has been revealed that “I just pick somewhere to start and go for it,” Bielfeldt explained. “You’re likely going to fail at first, and that’s what makes it even more interesting.”.

The experimentation and imperfection, he added, are the most interesting parts of the process and, ultimately, more notable to him than achieving the highest image quality.

Photo: Ole Bielfeldt/Nikon Small World.

Sources indicate that ah, mice; the humble martyrs to scientific progress. A significant amount of science seems to involve cutting up mice and learning from the result. But in this sort of photography, even the strongest mouse advocate must admit that the results are visually spectacular.

In a recent development, satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman of the University of Helsinki took this image of a mouse’s eye while researching drug therapy. Photo: Satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman/Nikon Small World.

Third place went to another rodent part: a 5X-magnified image of neurons in a mouse’s brain.

Photo: Kaelin Wulf and Rachel Flannery/Nikon Small World.

Recent findings suggest that in defense of humanity, we were also willing to subject our own body parts to photographic investigation. The 7th-place winner came from Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol at the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University. Using confocal imaging, which involves scanning a specimen to generate optical sections, they captured human neurons at 20X magnification.

These human neurons were grown from reprogrammed skin cells. Photo: Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol/Nikon Small World.

According to recent reports, I’ll end with a personal favorite of mine, John-Oliver Dum’s image of a little jumping spider, dusted with pollen. Dum, who won second place, credits a childhood bite for his fascination with spiders. The pollen was cultivated by his wife, specifically to create images like this one.

You can disagree, but I think this little guy is adorable. Photo: John-Oliver Dum.

Tech Report: Child and Dependent Care Credit – Middle-Income Families Now Get 35%, Up From 20%

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you pay for daycare, preschool, a nanny, or day camp so you can work, claim the child and dependent care credit when you file.
  • Your rate depends on your adjusted gross income (AGI), which is your total income minus certain adjustments.
  • For 2025, the rate fell to 20% once AGI passed $43,000.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you pay for daycare, preschool, a nanny, or day camp so you can work, claim the child and dependent care credit when you file. It’s worth 20% to 50% of up to $3,000 in care costs for one child under 13, or $6,000 for two or more, minus any tax-free dependent care benefits from work.

Your rate depends on your adjusted gross income (AGI), which is your total income minus certain adjustments. A 2025 tax law raised the rate for all but the highest incomes, starting with 2026 returns.

For 2025, the rate fell to 20% once AGI passed $43,000. For 2026, it’s 50% for an AGI of $15,000 or less and drops gradually to 35%, where it stays up to $150,000 on a joint return or $75,000 on any other return. Above that it drops again, to a floor of 20%.

Say two parents working full time, with a joint AGI of $120,000, pay $9,000 for two kids’ daycare. They count $6,000 of it, so at 35% the credit is $2,100, up from $1,200 at 2025’s 20%. It’s nonrefundable, so it can’t reduce your federal income tax below zero.

The care has to let you work or look for work, so if you’re married, you both need earnings unless one of you is a full-time student or disabled. The costs you count can’t be more than the lower earner’s earnings, and married couples must file jointly unless they lived apart for the last six months of the year.

Recent findings suggest that daycare, preschool, before- and after-school care, a nanny, and summer day camp count, as does care for a spouse or dependent who can’t care for themselves and lives with you more than half the year. Overnight camp and tuition for kindergarten and up don’t.

Every dollar your employer’s initiative covers tax-free, such as a dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), comes off your $3,000 or $6,000 limit. If that couple paid $5,000 of the daycare through an FSA, they could count only $1,000 of the other $4,000, for a $350 credit.

In a recent development, claim it on Form 2441 with your federal return. The form asks for each provider’s name, address, and taxpayer ID number, such as a daycare center’s employer identification number or a nanny’s Social Security number. Before you file, ask each provider for that number on Form W-10, the IRS’s request form, since leaving it off can cost you the credit.

Compare the best free tax software to find one that files Form 2441 with your return at no cost.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously.
  • But both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear.
  • The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously. One was studying to be a wildland firefighter, while the other hoped to become a mountain guide.

But both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear. Local authorities spent days looking for missing hikers Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20.

The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.

Matsuda and Donlon, students at Colorado Mountain College in Leadville, had planned on hiking and camping near Ice Mountain, a 13,960-foot peak located about 50 miles from Gunnison.

Sources indicate that they left for their trip on Oct. 23. College staff notified local authorities they were missing on Oct. 26, according to the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office. The men’s families said they were both experienced hikers.

Matsuda was studying to be a wildland firefighter, and Donlon was training to become a mountain guide.

According to recent reports, kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Sources indicate that search-and-rescue teams were deployed and found their vehicle at the trailhead. Weather conditions looked risky, with heavy snow falling in Chaffee County.

“Ice Mountain is a very technical climb, and it is recommended that hikers be very experienced when trying to tackle it. That is when it is dry. Although there was only about eight inches of snow around Kaden’s vehicle and in the lower basin, Ice Mountain received one to two feet of snow,” the sheriff’s office said in a Facebook post.

According to recent reports, multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Industry observers note that multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Rescue teams used drones, helicopters, and dogs to search for the two hikers. On October 27, they located their tent, which had collapsed under the weight of the snow, near West Apostle Mountain (13,597 feet). Inside were sleeping bags, stoves, and other equipment, but the two men were nowhere to be found.

The next day, authorities confirmed they had found their bodies in the mountain’s basin. Officials declined to share potential causes of death, beyond stating that they did not suspect foul play.

The Sawatch Range of the Rocky Mountains is home to many 13,000- and 14,000-foot peaks. Some of them, like West Apostle Mountain, require technical climbing ability and become substantially more difficult and dangerous during wet weather. The route up the mountain requires traversing fields of loose boulder scree and talus that can be hazardous after snow.

According to recent reports, from 2010 to 2017, eight people have died in the Sawatch Mountains. Falls are the most common cause of fatalities for those tackling Colorado’s 13ers and 14ers, as the state’s highest mountains are known to locals.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Part of a rock spire known as a fairy chimney collapsed yesterday near the entrance to one of Turkey’s most popular tourist destinations, killing three people and injuring five others.
  • In a recent development, the incident occurred around 3:15 pm local time in the town of Goreme, in central Turkey’s Cappadocia region yesterday.
  • Rescue teams initially recovered two bodies from the rubble before discovering a third victim overnight, bringing the death toll to three.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Part of a rock spire known as a fairy chimney collapsed yesterday near the entrance to one of Turkey’s most popular tourist destinations, killing three people and injuring five others.

In a recent development, the incident occurred around 3:15 pm local time in the town of Goreme, in central Turkey’s Cappadocia region yesterday. Rocks broke away and fell onto people near the parking area. The site is part of a UNESCO World Heritage landscape, famous for its cave dwellings and cone-shaped rock formations. Nevsehir Governor Huseyin Kok stated that heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that caused the rocks to detach from the formation, according to Reuters.

Rescue teams initially recovered two bodies from the rubble before discovering a third victim overnight, bringing the death toll to three. The deceased include two Turkish citizens and one foreign national. Five others were injured in the collapse. Some of them were later discharged from hospital, according to AFP.

Eyewitnesses described a loud noise followed by a large dust cloud. The area was closed to the public, and search operations concluded overnight under floodlights.

It has been revealed that turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek remarked an investigation by the chief prosecutor’s office, along with expert assessments, would begin. The collapse occurred on Turkey’s Republic Day, a public holiday when visitor numbers were high.

Cappadocia, in central Anatolia, is renowned for its distinctive fairy chimneys. These tall, thin spires of soft volcanic rock topped by harder caps were shaped over millions of years by wind and water erosion. The Goreme Open-Air Museum and surrounding sites were put on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1985 for their blend of natural landforms and human history, including Byzantine rock-cut churches and underground settlements. The region’s soft rock is geologically fragile and prone to weathering and occasional rockfalls, particularly after heavy rain.

Recent findings suggest that turkish authorities have previously carried out restoration and monitoring work to address erosion and climate-related risks, and smaller non-fatal collapses were recorded in the area in 2024 and 2025. The site remains one of Turkey’s most visited destinations, drawing tourists for hot-air balloon rides, hiking, and exploration of its unique geology and heritage.

The Shockingly Simple Math Behind Social Security

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most important things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.
  • Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who currently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.
  • But for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most important things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who currently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.

But for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future. We aren’t thinking about money that eases us into our Golden Years, we need something that starts working now. Plus we’d rather not rely on our government keeping its promises that far into the future.

It has been revealed that those were my thoughts in 2005, when I was just a young retiree myself. But a funny thing happens when time passes: you get older. And you realize that there are plenty of other older people around too. And suddenly, Social Security is an vital subject after all, that many people would like to know more about. But there is an endless pile of conflicting opinions:.

But when I did the math on all of this, I realized that it’s more confusing than it needs to be. Because when it comes to deciding on how Social Security fits into your retirement strategy, it really boils down to only one number:.

The Net Present Value of your future lifetime stream of Social Security payments.

That little piece of math jargon might not mean much if you don’t have fond memories of  Economics 101 class. But don’t worry, it’s easy to understand if you think of these two extremes:.

It has been revealed that if you want to retire in your 30s like I did, the value of your future Social Security is pretty close to zero. Even if the government keeps all of its promises, those payments are so far in the future that you need to save a full retirement ‘stash to get through the three decades until it kicks in.

On the other hand, if you’re already over 60 years old, contributed to Social Security throughout your long career and have a low cost of living, you may be eligible for payments that already meet all your needs.

Industry observers note that in this situation, you are set for life. Social Security will in theory cover all your needs and rise automatically with inflation, so you don’t have to save any additional money.

It has been revealed that in between these two extremes, the math gets interesting. Because while most people assume Social Security is useless until you reach full eligibility, the real story is that you can think of it as a chunk of money that you already have right now, which reduces the amount of saving you have to do on your own.

And there’s an easy way to calculate it, with an extremely useful thing called the Net Present Value calculation.

There’s an actual formula for this, but don’t worry you don’t have to memorize it because you can just have any Internet calculator, AI tool or spreadsheet do the math for you.

In a recent development, first let’s calculate the value a young couple might get if they do this calculation at 30 years old. We just have to make a few assumptions to have numbers plug into the formula:.

Recent findings suggest that when you plug in all the numbers and calculate this (the Net Present Value of a 30 year stream of income), the first number you’ll get is $667,166. But that’s not the final answer – that is how much you’d need if you wanted the payments to start right now.

The final step is applying a simpler version of the formula a second time, to account for the fact that you don’t need the money until 32 years from now:.

Industry observers note that at that point, you end up with a number around $98,280. But what does this mean?

It has been revealed that it means that if you stuck $98k into an investment account today and let it compound for 32 years, at that point it would be major enough to provide a stream of $4000 payments for the following 30 years. And this even takes future inflation into account!It also means that the 30 year old retirees can mark an imaginary $98k onto their “net worth” spreadsheet and save that much less. Or at least think of it as a nice safety margin.

Sources indicate that if you’re new to money and math, that may sound like sorcery, but if you’ve been investing for long enough you will understand that it really does work that way. So let’s re-run the example for a couple who is already 62 years old, and needs a $5000 income starting right now, that still needs to last 30 years.

That NPV calculation looks like this:.

And the answer is right around $834,000.

What this means, is that if they invested $834,000 into a fund that paid out 6% per year for 30 years before running dry, they’d get that exact same $5000 monthly income. And it would keep up with inflation.

It has been revealed that now that we’ve seen these examples from the extreme ends of the spectrum, we can see how this applies in a more typical situation. Here’s one that is loosely based on one from a real person I worked with last year:.

Shane Survivor is 55 and he has been through some hard times. He lost most of his savings in a business blowup a few years back, but really wishes he could still retire soon. His financial picture:.

It has been revealed that most financial advisors would tell him to tough it out and  just keep working until he hits Social Security eligibility. At least 62 to get the minimum benefits, but maybe even longer to get to Full Retirement Age (67) or even until 70 to get the maximum benefit.

But wait! Let’s do the math because who wants to work another fifteen years when you’re already tired of working at 55!

Industry observers note that shane logs into the Social Security website SSA.gov and uses the online tool to calculate what his payout will be. I just did this myself so we can use my numbers:.

Let’s start by calculating the Net Present Value of each of these three options for our 55-year old friend:.

According to recent reports, whoa wait a minute, that’s a counterintuitive result! Am I really telling you that it’s actually less valuable to work longer so you can get the higher benefits? The answer is yes, for people who understand the concepts of “investing” and “the time value of money”.

Sources indicate that to really understand this, just imagine what would happen if you started taking those payments as early as possible (age 62) and tossed them into an index fund, earning 6% after inflation on average. After the first year, you’d already have about $24,300 and you’d still be piling in that extra two grand per month and the whole snowball would be starting to compound.

It has been revealed that by the time your more patient friends started drawing $2796 payments five years later, you’d already have over $137,000. It’s such a massive lead that the 67-year-old will never catch up.

But let’s go back to Shane’s real situation and see if he can retire:.

According to recent reports, so the answer is no, not quite yet. But he’s closer than it looks: every year of additional work will have a triple effect because it will:.

As soon as his combined ‘stash investment income plus the Social Security payment reach $3000 per month, he’s done.

Industry observers note that and of course, any additional tricks he can apply like streamlining his spending and boosting his income, will make this even faster. I’d give him about three years before reaching liftoff.

So how can YOU use this information to speed up your own retirement?

According to recent reports, the net effect of Social Security is that it should help you worry a little less and work a little less. The worrying part should benefit everyone, and the working part is kind of a sliding scale:.

Can we just put this in ONE SIMPLE TABLE based on some reasonable assumptions?

Sources indicate that yes, absolutely! Just to hit the most common situation, let’s assume a household that has.

How much is this future benefit worth you you, based on your current age?

In a recent development, these aren’t enormous FAT Fire numbers, but every one of them is enough to feel like a meaningful contribution to your eventual early jump into freedom. For example as a 51-year-old, I can look at my number of roughly $350,000 and say yeah, that’s quite a big boost – enough to buy an entire house in many areas of the country or enough to fund multiple lifetimes of high-end groceries. And until now I had never even considered it as part of my retirement savings!

Frequently Asked (or Complained) Questions.

Now that we’ve covered the facts, I can already hear the complaints coming.

What if Social Security is canceled or greatly reduced by the time I reach that age?

Recent findings suggest that yeah, it might happen, but it’s also a top priority for most voters in our aging population. So it’s hard for politicians to make cuts. What is more likely is that the benefits will be cut for wealthier people. And if you find yourself in that camp (as I do), you won’t actually need the payments.

Sources indicate that sure, it’s not “fair”, but you know what? I can think of more fun ways to enjoy the fact that I’m a rich person rather than complaining about how some government program is “unfair”, and so can you.

Nobody can live on just a Social Security check!

First of all, millions of people do. In fact, last time I checked my own annual spending it was under $30k, most of it on optional luxuries, which is less than my expected payout!

But more importantly, most of us won’t have to, because we are also investing healthy sums on our own.

I’m still scared and worried about something else!

Now this is the root of the matter. In fact, worry is the root of almost all complications. And so that’s what we need to focus on in our future work. For some reason, I have managed to live the last twenty years pretty much completely free from financial worries, and I had assumed everyone else was the same way. But it turns out this is not the case, even among people much wealthier and more advantaged than I am.

So in the next article, we need to get into that.

Log yourself into ssa.gov, and if it’s your first time doing that – congratulations! Note that new users will need to create an account, and they’ll guide you to login.gov for that purpose. Don’t fret, it’s very useful to have this account for multiple reasons.

Bonus Materials: the Quirk of Social Security Contributions.

Industry observers note that to illustrate this point, I ran a simulation of two people who each make a $100k salary and contribute accordingly, but one retires after 10 years and that poor second guy works the full 35. Look at the difference in their benefits:.

So the early retiree only worked and contributed about 28% as much as the late retiree. But his benefits are still a much higher 45% of the big earner’s payouts. In summary? Social Security provides a mild incentive for slacking.

One other factor: after retiring earlier, you might still end up contributing more than you think. This is because any income you earn later in life through optional employment (or self employment) will trigger more contributions. In my 21 years of retirement, I have ended up earning and contributing more during about 15 of those years, bringing my average level up much higher than I originally expected.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain have completed the first ascent of 6,518m Jugal II.
  • According to Spanish media, the team climbed via the east-southeast side and reached the summit on October 26.
  • Jugal II was also the planned goal for Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet, who left for the area three weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain have completed the first ascent of 6,518m Jugal II.

According to Spanish media, the team climbed via the east-southeast side and reached the summit on October 26. One day later, they returned to base camp, their home team told Diario de Navarra. Zabalza and Urabain had explored the area in the spring of 2024, but bad weather prevented them from attempting the peak. The team will share more details when they’re back home.

Jugal II was also the planned goal for Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet, who left for the area three weeks ago. Originally, the team wanted to climb Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region. Recent storms and floods had cut trails and swept away bridges in that area, so they had to seek an alternative.

ExplorersWeb caught up with Meroi as she and Benet reached a lodge to seek shelter from the heavy rain.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re on our way to Kathmandu, and we are with the Spaniards,” she confirmed. As Nives explained, they all attempted the climb, and the Spanish team reached the summit, while the Italians retreated on the previous day. Until now, there has been no news from the Italians since Tine Cuder of Slovenia, the third team member, fell ill and left the expedition two weeks ago.

Sources indicate that left to right, Nives Meroi, Tine Cuder, and Romano Benet in Kathmandu. Photo: Romano Benet.

It has been revealed that the Jugal Himal is just northeast of Kathmandu, on the Tibetan border. Surprisingly accessible for a previously unclimbed peak, it’s reachable by bus and a few days’ trekking. Jugal I and II opened to foreign expeditions in 2023. In spring 2024, veteran South Korean climber Um Hong-gil led a Korean-Nepalese expedition featuring Sherpa celebrities Dawa Yangzum and Lakpa Dendi to both unclimbed Jugals. They successfully summited Jugal I, but not Jugal II. According to The Himalayan Database, Jugal II remained unclimbed.

It has been revealed that the main peaks in Jugal Himal. Photo: Nepali News Hub.

Piolets d'Or Insider: How the Jury Works, Style Debates, and Future Looks

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1131 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The recent 2026 edition of the Piolets d’Or awards, held last week in a remote corner of the French Alps, felt like an organization trying to adapt to fast-changing times and attract larger audiences while keeping its prestige and spirit intact.
  • According to recent reports, explorersWeb was there to meet old acquaintances and to put a face to some of the names we wrote about in the last 12 months.
  • Recent findings suggest that views of Les Ecrins Massif from Saint-Christophe-en-Oisans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The recent 2026 edition of the Piolets d’Or awards, held last week in a remote corner of the French Alps, felt like an organization trying to adapt to fast-changing times and attract larger audiences while keeping its prestige and spirit intact.

According to recent reports, explorersWeb was there to meet old acquaintances and to put a face to some of the names we wrote about in the last 12 months. We also wanted to participate in the collective exercise of reflection about the future.

Recent findings suggest that views of Les Ecrins Massif from Saint-Christophe-en-Oisans. Photo: Angela Benavides.

Piolet d’Or recipients enjoyed a relaxed atmosphere at the tiny village of Saint-Christophe-en-Oisans and a ceremony at Burg d’Oisans, a 30-minute drive down the valley. Yet, the most interesting event took place the following day, as an elite group of climbers sat around a table in a small hall with large glass windows facing autumn-colored forests and the ragged peaks of the Ecrins Massif, covered in the first snow dust of the season.

Representing the awardees were Nicolas Jean (awarded for climbing Jannu East with Benjamin Vedrines); the complete teams from Ultar Shar, Aikache Chokk, and Jerupaja Grande; a hyper-energetic, widely smiling Peter Habeler, 84, who received a lifetime achievement Piolet d’Or; Simon Welfringer, who gave a talk; organizers Christian Trommsdorf and David Chambre; geographer and chronicler Rodolphe Popier, and two members of the jury: Jordi Corminas of Spain and Paul Ramsden of the UK. At a press conference, these experts debated some of the hot problems in today’s mountaineering.

According to recent reports, simon Welfringer of France speaks at the post-Piolets d’Or experts’ panel. Photo: Angela Benavides.

Sources indicate that trommsdorf noted that the jury had an easy time selecting the awarded climbs this year. He explained how these expert jurists choose the best alpine-style activities of the year.

The members work remotely, choosing from a Big List of outstanding activities. This list is previously compiled by Lindsay Griffin, long-time editor of the American Alpine Journal, and the UK’s Alpine Club. Jurors study the climbs and narrow it down to a short list of candidates, which is not made public. The awards go to those activities chosen by the majority of jury members. In this case, decisions were finalized on the first vote, with no need for a tie-break.

Left to right, Rodolphe Popier, Jordi Corominas, Paul Ramsden (speaking), and David Chambre. Photo: Piotr Drozdz.

That led to the first topic of debate: It was noted that some climbing teams happily announce themselves as “Piolet d’Or nominates” on social media when their climbs appear on the Big List — although organizers make it clear that not all activities on that list are suitable for a Piolet d’Or. Yet, no one supported the idea of making the short lists public. The general agreement was to keep the small “best of the year” finalists available only to the jury.

It has been revealed that the second topic for debate was the presence of a relatively new piece of technology now ubiquitous on expeditions: drones. These have become essential on rescues, but climbing teams also use them to scout the route ahead. In the near future, drones could also carry supplies, emergency kits, or extra equipment. Commercial outfitters are already using them in this way.

In a recent development, benjamin Vedrines and Nicolas Jean of France used drones to check the state of their planned route on Jannu. However, they explained that the drone was useless in relaying information about a section that they couldn’t see from Base Camp. It had a different angle of view, and the drone lost connection when it tried to approach that area.

Drones piloted by their base camp film crew also hovered overhead as they traversed the long summit ridge. Finally, before the summit push, they used drones to clearly identify the highest point, to make sure they reached the true summit.

The Ultar Sar team also had a drone, they noted. All the awarded climbers agreed that drones are okay as long as the climbers are completely transparent about what they used them for. Jordi Corominas mentioned the drones are a technological innovation that has come to stay, no different than InReach devices, satphones, or even ice axes and crampons.

Jordi Corominas, left, discusses past climbs with Benjamin Vedrines. Photo: Piotr Drozdz.

Interestingly, one jurist stood against the tide: Paul Ramsden is an advocate for the pure alpine-style criteria of the UK climbing school, and with five Piolets d’Or, he is the overall record holder of these prestigious awards. In his opinion, drones spoil the adventure and uncertainty inherent in pure alpine style. Ramsden himself uses neither drones, trackers, nor even satphones.

Finally, Trommsdor suggested possibly expanding the awards to create a special Piolet d’Or for the best rock climb and perhaps even the best ski descent. The idea expand on the newly introduced performance category introduced this year in the big list as a test. The category featured, among others, the two Everest ski descents in 2025. Both were heavily supported, and Jim Morrison‘s descent of the Hornbein Couloir was oxygen-assisted.

In the end, one of the performance ski descents received the female award: Typhaine Duperier‘s alpine-style climb+ski descent of Nanga Parbat’s Schell route, with Boris Langenstein.

It is unclear whether the new additions will become official in the near future, but some attendees expressed concern about the context in which these take place. Would they award ski expeditions for their boldness or technical excellence without bearing in mind how the skiers reached the start of their descent (supported climbs, fixed routes, even helicopters)?

As for rock climbs: where to set the difference between a rock climb and an alpine climb on high, but dry, faces? The debate was left open. We will find out what, if anything, changes in the next edition of the Piolets d’Or.

Buried houses at the now abandoned village of La Berarde. Photo: Piotr Drozdz.

The physical award is no longer an actual piolet (ice axe). In the last few years, it has been a hand-crafted trophy that changes with the venue. This time, it was a plaque with a reproduction of Ecrins National Park’s most distinctive peak, La Meige. It rested on a piece of rock from the remains of La Berarde, a nearby village destroyed in a flood two years ago.

Recent findings suggest that at the Piolets d’Or ceremony in Burg d’Oisans. Photo: Angela Benavides.

Industry observers note that next year, the Piolets d’Or will be staged in the same location, perhaps in late summer. The event will commemorate the 150th anniversary of the first ascent of La Meige. The long-term plan is to turn the Piolet d’Or ceremony into a bigger, international mountain festival.

Adventurer to Climb 100 Peaks on 2,000Km Taiwan Traverse

📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tomorrow, November 1, Japanese adventurer Yoki Tanaka begins a four-month, 2,000km trek north to south down the length of Taiwan.
  • According to recent reports, taiwan has about 268 peaks exceeding 3,000m, but only 100 of them made this special list, which is based not only on height but beauty, difficulty, prominence, and character.
  • It has been revealed that yoki Tanaka arrives in Taiwan earlier this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tomorrow, November 1, Japanese adventurer Yoki Tanaka begins a four-month, 2,000km trek north to south down the length of Taiwan. Along the way, he will summit all 100 of Taiwan’s celebrated Baiyue peaks.

According to recent reports, taiwan has about 268 peaks exceeding 3,000m, but only 100 of them made this special list, which is based not only on height but beauty, difficulty, prominence, and character. Prominent Taiwanese mountaineers compiled the list in the early 1970s, partly inspired by Japan’s own list of 100 revered mountains.

It has been revealed that yoki Tanaka arrives in Taiwan earlier this week. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

Sources indicate that the 43-year-old Tanaka has specialized in this unusual combination of long-distance trekking and mountaineering. In 2014, he summited Japan’s 100 famous mountains while walking 7,800km over 208 days. (Japan, though far bigger than Taiwan, has only 23 mountains over 3,000m.) A year later, he extended that by climbing 200 mountains and walking 8,000km in 222 days. Finally, he increased that again to 300 mountains. This time, it took him three years and about 20,000km of walking.

Tanaka’s projected route across Taiwan.

Tanaka will begin on Sunday from the northernmost tip of Taiwan, at the Cape Fugui lighthouse, and finish sometime in March at Eluanbi, the country’s southernmost point. The first 150km will be along roads before he reaches his first trailhead. He’ll spend the next week trekking. His first five peaks will be Xueshan (3,886m), Nanhudashan (3,742m), Hehuanshan (3,417m), Qilaishan (3,560m), and Nenggaoshan 3,262m).

Although he won’t use motorized transport for the entire journey, he will have ample opportunity to resupply along the way. His expedition strategy includes a charmingly precise breakdown of how he intends to spend his evenings: town stays, 48 days; mountain huts, 38 days; tent camping, 39 days. He has also budgeted 16 rest days and 20 contingency days.

Tanaka trains in Taiwan earlier this year. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that his most difficult section, scheduled for early January, will take him through the remote interior of the Central Mountain Range for over two weeks. During this time, he’ll have to carry his own food, search for trails that may no longer exist, and gamble that he will be able to find enough water.

During a December 2025 reconnaissance trip to Xueshan, Taiwan’s second-highest mountain, Tanaka discovered how difficult it can be to obtain water. Two water sources marked on his map were completely dry.

It has been revealed that on a previous hike. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

By late January, the Japanese trekker should reach the historic Batongguan Trail, eventually leading to 3,952m Yushan, Taiwan’s highest mountain. The Batongguan Trail was originally constructed in 1875 under the Qing dynasty to establish a route across the mountainous interior. Decades later, Japanese colonial authorities constructed a separate crossing through the region. Sections of the route survive as remote hiking trails and provide access to some of Taiwan’s highest mountains.

Tanaka first visited Taiwan in the spring of 2025 and has made several reconnaissance visits since, including an east-west crossing of the island earlier this year. He had intended to begin his Taiwan 100 Peaks Traverse project this past spring, but local mountaineers advised him to avoid the rainy season and typhoon risks. Their advice prompted him to shift his starting date to November.

According to recent reports, yoki Tanaka on a training hike in Taiwan. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

Interestingly, of Taiwan’s 100 Baiyue peaks, only 99 are now recognized as surpassing 3,000m. The exception is Lushan at 2,981m. It was originally measured at 3,043m but subsequent measurements reduced its elevation. Nevertheless, it remains on the list.

Taiwan’s representative in Japan told Japanese media that the fastest prior completion of the Baiyue by a foreign climber took three years and eight months, spread over multiple trips.

Once Tanaka begins, his expedition website will provide live tracking of his progress across Taiwan.
